title: Уловка с чужой палатой  (The Decoy Hospital Room Trick)

segments.t: Knowing that Sasha is waiting for him inside his real room, Max frantically steers Vika into a neighboring ward down the hall and climbs into an empty bed. Back at the bar, Vika had pressured Kostya into revealing which hospital Max was taken to.
Вот сюда.
Я смотрю, ты не рад, что я пришла?
Как не рад?
Кстати, а как ты узнала, что я здесь?
Костя сказал.
Костя, в какой больнице лежит Макс?
Я не знаю.
Так, почему у тебя кофемашина грязная?
Тебя штрафовать?
Я вообще только что кофе сделал.
А где все апельсины?
Ты вино заказал?
В какой больнице, Макс?
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
Вот сюда.
'Right in here.' The grammar packs 'there you go' and 'here' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Я смотрю, ты не рад, что я пришла?
'I see you are not glad that I came?' Kostya anchors the line on 'I', while 'came' completes the thought.
Как не рад?
'What do you mean not glad?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'how' and finishing on 'glad'. Kostya answers right away.
Кстати, а как ты узнала, что я здесь?
'By the way, how did you find out that I was here?' The grammar packs 'by the way' and 'here' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Костя сказал.
'Kostya told me.' Max anchors the line on 'Kostya', while 'to say' completes the thought.
Костя, в какой больнице лежит Макс?
'Kostya, which hospital is Max in?' Kostya raises the pitch on 'Max' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Max answers right away.
Я не знаю.
'I do not know.' The grammar packs 'I' and 'know' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Так, почему у тебя кофемашина грязная?
'All right, why is your coffee machine dirty?' Kostya anchors the line on 'like this', while 'dirty' completes the thought.
Тебя штрафовать?
'Should I fine you?' In Russian, the idea of 'you' flows naturally into 'to fine' without extra filler words. Kostya answers right away.
Я вообще только что кофе сделал.
'I literally just made coffee.' In Russian, the idea of 'I' flows naturally into 'to do' without extra filler words.
А где все апельсины?
'And where are all the oranges?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'and' before landing on 'oranges'.
Ты вино заказал?
'Did you order the wine?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'you' before landing on 'ordered'. Max answers right away.
В какой больнице, Макс?
'Which hospital is Max in?' The meaning hinges on 'what' working together with 'Max' in spoken Russian. Alright, let's listen to all those lines again from the top.
